commentary: I re-graded the walk set unnarrowed, all three walks. The supersession-notice entry from the second walk now holds, because the third walk's trail-read condition completes it. I checked that condition against the engine rather than the harness. Exactly one landed member with no walk naming it is the engine's PAIR-OPEN one-landed row before the ENDED rule applies. An apply later than that member is exactly what drops it from the fresh list. So the notice fires where the engine's own stale presentation row would, whatever clause the reason names. The only mention of the reason left in either body is the sentence saying not to use it. The residual diff from the external return's commit lies entirely inside the three walks' edit records. One imprecision from the last pass still stands and is unchanged: the bodies pick the external member by filename, which cannot tell a reader-rejected hand-saved return from an accepted one. orbit external save never writes such a file.
